title: Étale local identification of regular boundary components with coordinate hyperplanes
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $D\hookrightarrow X$ be a reduced closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose that $D_1,\ldots,D_m$ are exactly the distinct irreducible components of $D$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], each with its reduced induced scheme structure, and that every $D_a$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $v:W\to X$ be étale [def-weil-etale-morphism], let $w\in W$, and set $x=v(w)$. Assume that $R=\mathcal O_{W,w}$ is a regular local ring of dimension $d$, and choose a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], meaning $d$ elements generating the maximal ideal of $R$. Choose regular functions representing these germs on an open neighborhood $V$ of $w$. For $0\le r\le d$, suppose that $D\times_X V=V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ as closed subschemes of $V$ (the empty product is $1$). Here the coordinate hyperplane with index $i$ means the closed subscheme $V(t_i)\subset V$. Then, after shrinking $V$ around $w$, there is a bijection $\{a:x\in D_a\}\simeq\{1,\ldots,r\}$, written $a\mapsto i(a)$, such that $D_a\times_X V=V(t_{i(a)})$ for every $a$ with $x\in D_a$; for all other $a$ the pullback is empty. Consequently every scheme-theoretic intersection of selected $D_a$ pulls back to the intersection of their assigned coordinate hyperplanes, or is empty if a selected component misses $x$. Every generic point of a nonempty irreducible component of $D_a\times_XW$ maps to the generic point of $D_a$.

proof.text: Remove from $V$ the inverse images of the finitely many $D_a$ missing $x$; these closed subsets miss $w$. Apply [lem-trf-regular-component-etale-stalk-primes] at $w$. In $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}\to R$ the retained component ideals $\mathfrak p_a$ are distinct minimal primes over the boundary ideal $I$; their extensions $\mathfrak q_a$ are proper primes contracting to $\mathfrak p_a$, and $V(IR)=\bigcup_aV(\mathfrak q_a)$.

source.place: Tag 07NF, lemma-regular-goes-up; agent local-component application and contraction argument of returned parent steps 1--3 (full argument and other source nodes retained in report.md).

proof.text: The given equality of closed subschemes gives $IR=(T)$ for $T=t_1\cdots t_r$. The finite family indexed by $F_x=\{a:x\in D_a\}$ has distinct minimal contractions $\mathfrak p_a$, proper prime extensions $\mathfrak q_a$ and the covering $V((T))=\bigcup_{a\in F_x}V(\mathfrak q_a)$ by Step 1. With the regular local ring $R$ and its full parameter system, these are the hypotheses of [lem-trf-parameter-product-prime-family-matching]. It gives the bijection $a\mapsto i(a)$ and $\mathfrak q_a=(t_{i(a)})$, with both indexing sets empty when $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AG0, lemma-regular-local-UFD, opening proof that parameter elements are prime; agent prime-family matching argument of returned parent steps 4--6.

proof.text: The étale morphism is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $W$, and thus $V$, locally Noetherian. For the finite family of retained pullbacks $D_a\times_X V$ and the closed subschemes $V(t_{i(a)})$, the stalk ideals at $w$ agree by Step 2. Apply [lem-trf-closed-subscheme-germ-family-spreading] to obtain one open neighbourhood on which every equality holds. The removed pullbacks remain empty.

source.place: Tag 01Y3, lemma-local-isomorphism, neighbourhood principle; agent finite-generator ideal-equality and intersection version of returned parent steps 7--8.

proof.text: Scheme-theoretic intersection is the fibre product of the closed immersions, so by the universal property of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] the pullback along $U\to X$ of the intersection of selected $D_a$ is the intersection in $U$ of their pullbacks $D_a\times_XU$. Apply the intersection clause of [lem-trf-closed-subscheme-germ-family-spreading] on that neighbourhood $U$: a selection of retained components has ideal $(t_{i(a)}:a\text{ selected})$. A selection containing a removed component maps to its empty pullback, so it has unit ideal and is empty. The empty selection has zero ideal and gives the whole neighbourhood. This proves all scheme-theoretic intersection assertions.

source.place: Tag 01Y3, lemma-local-isomorphism, neighbourhood principle; agent finite-generator ideal-equality and intersection version of returned parent steps 7--8.

proof.text: For the final assertion use the full pullback $E_a=D_a\times_X W$, before any shrinking. Its projection $p:E_a\to D_a$ is étale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], hence flat [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The reduced irreducible scheme $D_a$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]; let $\eta$ be its generic point [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Let $z$ be the generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of an irreducible component $C$ of $E_a$. As $\overline{\{\eta\}}=D_a$, $\eta$ specializes to $p(z)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] gives $z'\in E_a$ specializing to $z$ with $p(z')=\eta$. Then $\overline{\{z'\}}$ is irreducible and contains $\overline{\{z\}}=C$; maximality of the component [def-weil-irreducible-components] gives $\overline{\{z'\}}=C$, and uniqueness of generic points [lem-sc-scheme-sober] gives $z'=z$. Hence $p(z)=\eta$.
